outcome: Incidence of spinal anesthesia induced hypotension
cohort: Participants undergoing cesarean section under spinal anesthesia, predominantly aged 25-30.
finding: Co-loading was found to be a better strategy for preventing spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension in Cesarean section patients, leading to a lower incidence of hypotension and reduced vasopressor usage compared to preloading or no-loading.
mod_finding: Co-loading was identified as a superior strategy for preventing hypotension during spinal anesthesia for cesarean sections, a specific mode of birth.
